action_items: Marcus: provision benchmark harness and run sample TGI/vLLM parity tests against customer's prompts — due 2026-09-14
Lena: send pricing bands and reserved capacity options, include burst/overage rules — due 2026-09-09

meeting_header: Date: 2026-09-07 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 57m | Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Seastar Head of ML), Owen Blake (Platform), Sara Kim (Security)
summary: Discovery call to assess feasibility of migrating Seastar's inference stack (currently a mix of OpenAI hosted + on-prem vLLM/TGI) to Redwood. Primary concerns: latency at scale, eval parity, private VPC/on-prem needs for models containing regulated data, and price predictability. Agreed to run a 72-hour hosted eval using Seastar's prompt corpus and for Redwood SE to produce quantization and Dedicated capacity estimates. Security/SSO/KMS questions to be followed up by Sara.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Security: SOC2 / SSO / KMS / data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Lena: ok hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i'll do quick intros. i'm lena, account exec at Redwood. Marcus with me from SE.
[00:10] Priya: hi, i'm priya, head of ml at seastar. we run most models in a mix right now, openai for convo stuff and vllm/tgi in our platform for higher throughput batch scoring.
[00:22] Marcus: great, thanks. quick clarifying q: when you say vllm/tgi in the platform, are you running both in prod or is t g i just for experiments?
[00:32] Owen: it's mixed. vllm is our low latency path for in-prod, TGI for experimentation and some batch offline scoring, so not fully homogeneous.
[00:40] Sara: and security wise, some datasets are regulated so they can't leave our VPC without controls.
[00:45] Lena: totally, that's exactly the sort of constraint we want to surface. today's goals: understand your success criteria, what parity means for you, and tradeoffs for hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:58] Priya: parity for us means 1) same token-level output distribution for our prompts (or within acceptable delta), 2) end-to-end p95 latency under X ms for interactive flows, 3) cost per 1M tokens comparable to or better than current effective cost.
[01:14] Marcus: good — when you say "same output distribution" are you capturing eval sets / test harness?
[01:20] Priya: yes we have a 8k prompt corpus with automated checks and human review on a sample. we'll share that.
[01:26] Lena: excellent. quick question on throughput: what's your typical QPS for the conversational product vs batch?
[01:33] Owen: conv is about 120 qps during peak, batch jobs peak at 3k requests but can be sharded and aren't latency sensitive.
[01:40] Marcus: thank you. that helps with batching/instancing discussion. latencies you mentioned — p95 target?
[01:46] Priya: target p95 is 200ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens). tail meeting there is currently spiky with vllm under load.
[01:54] Marcus: under load spikes are usually Kv cache and batching behavior — we can discuss runtime tuning. our serving runtime does continuous batching and prefix caching, though with private deployments kernel selection can change.
[02:07] Owen: can you explain the dedicated option vs hosted in terms of isolation and burst? we like predictability but sometimes need bursts.
[02:16] Lena: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and guaranteed capacity, plus the option for controlled burst capacity. Hosted is multi-tenant with fast onboarding and cost flexibility. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for regulated data that must remain in your network and integrates with your KMS/HSM.
[02:33] Sara: on KMS and audit logs — do you integrate with customer KMS and provide tamper-evident audit logs?
[02:39] Marcus: yes we integrate with customer-managed KMS for Private. For Dedicated and Hosted we support envelope encryption, with Dedicated offering options for customer key material in some cases. Audit logs and SSO/SAML are available; we provide per-request traces in the console.
[02:53] Priya: ok cool. another big question: model compatibility. we rely on some custom TGI ops and patches. how often do you run into model ops mismatch when onboarding?
[03:04] Marcus: short answer: it depends. we've onboarded models with custom kernels before. Redwood's runtime has kernel selection heuristics and we provide a compatibility shim for common TGI/vLLM variants. occasionally we need small model surgery — quantization-friendly changes or ensuring attention pattern compatibility.
[03:20] Priya: that's worrying; can you quantify how often surgery was needed?
[03:24] Marcus: i'd say in ~20% of cases for bleeding-edge forks, but for mainstream HF-style models and common TGI builds it's closer to 5-8%.
[03:33] Owen: what about vLLM specifically — we use vLLM's async batching; what happens to semantics if we move to Redwood's runtime?
[03:41] Marcus: we mimic async semantics, but batching strategies differ; you'll want to run parity tests. we also support KV cache semantics we call "prefix/KV cache" that preserves continuity for streaming scenarios.
[03:52] Priya: ok, so the parity plan would be what — run the corpus on both systems, compare token diffs and latencies?
[03:58] Marcus: yes, our recommended approach: 1) run your eval corpus on Redwood hosted to get baseline token outputs and latency profiles, 2) run on Dedicated if you want capacity-estimates under reservation constraints, 3) we'll produce a parity report with diffs and recommend quantization/opt changes.
[04:15] Lena: we'll also include quality regression alerts setup and an eval harness so you can re-run after model updates.
[04:22] Sara: on the hosted eval, any PII concerns? what data can we send for the 72-hour trial?
[04:28] Lena: good question — we can provide a secure upload path and advise anonymization. For regulated data we'd recommend Private deployment or using tokenized redaction in the eval. we'll be explicit in the migration checklist.
[04:40] Priya: cost modeling — how granular is token-level cost reporting? we need to attribute to product features.
[04:46] Marcus: we provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the Console with per-route views. You can tag requests and get per-feature billing estimates.
[04:55] Owen: curious on quantization — we currently run int8 on vLLM, can Redwood runtime do int4/in8 etc and what's the impact?
[05:03] Marcus: we support multiple quantization profiles; int8 is widely supported and int4 is possible with some accuracy tradeoffs depending on model. We'll run a small ablation; typically int4 reduces memory footprint substantially but can need recalibration on your eval set.
[05:17] Priya: when you say "need recalibration" do you mean finetune or just change inference config?
[05:21] Marcus: typically inference config and sometimes slight calibration steps; rarely need a finetune.
[05:25] Lena: switching to procurement/contract concerns — is timeline tied to any procurement windows?
[05:30] Priya: yes, we have an internal budget cycle end of october. ideal to have pilot and initial outcomes by mid-oct to inform Q4 budgets.
[05:40] Lena: good to know. we'll aim to have the hosted eval results + cost estimates before then.
[05:45] Owen: how does Redwood handle fallbacks if a model variant fails in Dedicated — auto degrade to smaller model?
[05:51] Marcus: you can set routing policy with fallbacks to compatible model variants or regions. Redwood supports canary and automatic rollback policies.
[06:00] Sara: on compliance, do you have SOC2 type 2 and ISO certifications?
[06:05] Lena: Redwood is SOC2 type 2 and working toward ISO — we will include the certs in the pack.
[06:11] Priya: do you have examples with customers in fintech or health for private deployments?
[06:16] Lena: yes, we have case studies for private deployments in regulated industries; i'll send redacted references.
[06:22] Marcus: quick technical Q from me — what's the longest sequence length you need and typical context window?
[06:27] Priya: we sometimes use long context up to 8k for multi-doc summarization. most conv flows are <512.
[06:33] Marcus: good, that affects kernel selection and memory planning. We'll include recommendations for compaction or chunking for long contexts.
[06:41] [07:00] (small cross-talk and background noise)
[07:08] Owen: can we talk about SLAs — what does Redwood guarantee on latency and uptime for Dedicated?
[07:14] Marcus: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency SLOs; we'll share the SLA doc. For hosted we provide best-effort latency targets in the perf profile.
[07:23] Priya: is there a minimum commitment for Dedicated?
[07:27] Lena: yes Dedicated typically has monthly/annual reserved capacity contracts. pricing varies by GPU type and commitment term. we'll include examples.
[07:36] Sara: from security side, integration with our SSO, SCIM, RBAC model — how granular can RBAC be?
[07:44] Marcus: pretty granular — token-level scoping, per-route roles and auditing. SCIM/SSO provisioning is supported.
[07:51] Priya: another issue: we've built internal wrappers and tools around vLLM's internal APIs, so switch would require engineering effort. can you support a migration runbook?
[08:01] Lena: yes we'll provide a migration runbook and an onboarding plan with milestones and expected engineering FTE.
[08:08] Owen: for the hosted eval, do you collect logs for us to analyze? we want to correlate tail latency with request patterns.
[08:14] Marcus: yes we capture request traces, token timing, and you can stream logs to your logging endpoint or S3.
[08:20] Priya: what's the worst-case delta you've seen in outputs when porting models from vLLM to another runtime?
[08:27] Marcus: worst case for tricky custom ops might be larger diffs, but for mainstream models diffs are often small — think sentence-level paraphrase differences not functionally breaking. Again parity run needed.
[08:38] Lena: any blockers we haven't covered?
[08:41] Sara: we need encryption in transit + at rest with customer-managed keys for Private. Also legal requires shared responsibility matrix.
[08:50] Lena: we'll send a responsibility matrix template and KMS integration notes.
[08:55] Priya: ok timeline recap: we want pilot results mid-october, security review early next week maybe.
[09:03] Lena: sounds good. do we want to schedule a dedicated SE deep dive on quantization and kernel tuning?
[09:07] Priya: yes please — maybe next week.
[09:10] Marcus: i'll propose two slots, one focused on quantization/throughput and one on eval harness integration.
[09:16] (conversation continues with specific probing on memory/instance sizes, cost math)
[09:25] Marcus: to give a concrete example — for 120 qps conversational with p95 200ms and 512 token context, we typically recommend X GPUs with continuous batching; exact numbers after we profile your corpus.
[09:36] Owen: can you do that profile with our corpus as part of the hosted eval?
[09:39] Marcus: yes, we'll include the profiler run.
[09:42] Priya: any considerations for multi-region routing, we have users in EU and NA?
[09:49] Lena: Redwood supports routing by region and model routing policies; we can set region failover. data residency options available for Private.
[09:58] Sara: also need to check logging retention and access controls for audit; legal needs that spelled out.
[10:04] Lena: understood, we'll include retention options in the security packet.
[10:08] (background typing)
[10:14] Priya: one last question on observability — can we get per-token breakdown and anomaly alerts on quality regressions?
[10:20] Marcus: yes Redwood Optimize and Console can alert on eval set regressions; we can hook QA signals to trigger rollbacks.
[10:26] Lena: ok i'll summarize next steps now.
[10:29] Lena: action items: Marcus will run parity harness on customer prompts for hosted; Marcus and Priya will align on dataset; Lena to send pricing/committed capacity examples and security pack; Sara to share security questions and data residency reqs. we'll aim for hosted eval to start early next week, results within 72 hours of run.
[10:49] Priya: that works. thanks everyone.
[10:52] Owen: thanks.
[10:54] Lena: thanks all, talk soon.
[10:57] (call ends)
closing_notes: Recap delivered verbally at end of call. Agreed pilot window and deliverables. Redwood to follow up with docs and benchmark plan. Security to get SOC2/arch + KMS notes. SE to schedule quantization deep dive next week.
